summary: This was our second game on Cape Violet: three Cortex seats against thebluegecko. On our side of the map we out-expanded him: 37 extractors by 10:16, 12 of them on under-water spots taken by Muskrats, and none of his extractors was ever seen. By 14:00 the three seats' army was 24.8k against 1.7k of his seen. But all of it went by land into his B3 nest, which sits on the only land passage. Twin Guards repaired by construction turrets, then Sumos and Mammoths, took 5.6k for 0.5k by 10:16 and 16.1k for 3.8k in the three minutes to 17:04. Meanwhile he took the sea and climbed the tech: his torpedo launchers killed 11 of our sea extractors from 11:02 with none answered, a Despot battleship sat in the central lake from 19:56, Shivas came from 18:02, and Wasps and a cruise-missile ship arrived by 25:00. We had no ship, plane or anti-air all game, and his Shivas and Wasps broke the bases at 24:30-26:00. The user's verdict was that the early economic lead was never converted into damage, and that air or naval units were needed early, or siege units used properly.

root.what: The player saw his lab on the B3 passage, the only land way west, and planned to break it by land with tier-1 tanks. The 'shipyard decision at ~2:30' from 0:05 lapsed, although the brief in force said to build a shipyard by 4:00 and never to walk into the B3 camp. From here the leads went into the one place he was strongest, and the sea, his road and his economy, was left to him (person-backed: the user, 25:40).

their_play: thebluegecko played Cortex alone. His bot lab stood on the B3 passage, the only land way into his half, by 2:31, with a Guard, Twin Guards and Grunts. Construction turrets behind the Twin Guards repaired them under our attacks and reclaimed our wrecks (the user at 10:05 and 10:14). His construction ships were at our coast from about 7:10, and the torpedo launchers they laid killed our under-water extractors from 11:02. He had tier 2 by 8:49 (an Advanced Construction Bot), Sumos from 10:05, and Mammoths holding B3 from about 14:41. Shivas (tier-3 amphibious) followed from 18:02, a Despot battleship in the central lake from 19:56, and by 24:55-25:25 construction aircraft, 18-19 Wasps and a Messenger cruise-missile ship. On land he never came out beyond Sumo sorties (12 died at spot_31 13:48-14:24). He fought on his towers, then came by water and air into our bases at 22:00-26:00. None of his extractors or his main base beyond B3 was ever in our sight.

Twin Guards repaired by construction turrets beat tier-1 tanks at every try. The long-range answer came as 2 Tremors, at 14:24 and after.
Our massed tier-1 land army told him he was safe to tech: tier 2 by 8:49, Shivas by 18:02, a Despot, Wasps and a cruise-missile ship.

lens.caveats: No truth file, so his numbers are floors: his extractors and economy were never seen, and minutes.py's HIS TIER 2 section is empty though corack was seen at 8:49. minutes.py, analyze_match.py, floor.py and raid_ledger.py read only the first record (seat 0). I ran them on seats 1 and 2 through scratch directories that symlink record-N as record-0; the opponent columns are shared sight. analyze_match.py's engagements are per seat; the side's trade figures come from the player's report ('each death counted once across our seats'). pro_baseline.py was not run (not Comet). The batch has no ledger row and no review.md. The lobby script says thebluegecko was Armada, but the records show Cortex units, and the player believed Armada until 2:45. Result minute: the records end at 26:06; the outcome is inferred from the user's verdict and two commander deaths. chat.jsonl carries the user's 25:40 line twice; it is listed once here. Loss on a since-fixed defect: only the 5:14 Incisor loss (about 1k) rests on the cannot-fire gap, fixed the same day. The loss rests on the strategy (land sieges, no sea or air) and on the idle hover platforms, which are not shown fixed.

open_questions: Why did both hover platforms stay idle for 11 minutes with a Cayman-only list (the pick kept 'nothing' at Cayman ratings of 0.15-0.35), and does a lab with a player's list still idle this way today?

The brief in force said to build a shipyard by 4:00 and never to walk into the B3 camp. Why did the player defer the shipyard ('decision at ~2:30') and then drop it? Did the brief's water lines reach the turn, or were they outweighed by the land plan?
How many sea spots did he hold, and when? We never saw one of his extractors, and there is no truth file.
What killed the two shipyard frames (12:11 at (7280, 4800) and 21:48 at (5824, 1840)) out of sight: torpedo launchers, the Despot, or submarines?
Did the player's belief that he was Armada (0:05-2:45) shape the opening (Incisors chosen to 'beat Grunts', the D2/D4 shallows route)?
